title: The Surly Guest
author: James Baldwin
summary: 脾气暴躁的伦道夫不肯告诉客栈老板去向，结果迷了路。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1912 by the American Book Company; author James Baldwin (1841–1925). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: One day John Randolph, of Roanoke, set out on horseback to ride to a town that was many miles from his home. The road was strange to him, and he traveled very slowly.
paragraphs.zh: 一天，罗阿诺克的约翰·伦道夫骑马出发，要去一个离家很多英里的城镇。路他不熟，所以走得很慢。

paragraphs.en: When night came on he stopped at a pleasant roadside inn and asked for lodging. The innkeeper welcomed him kindly. He had often heard of the great John Randolph, and therefore he did all that he could to entertain him well.
paragraphs.zh: 夜幕降临时，他在一家舒适的路边客栈停下，要求住宿。客栈老板热情地欢迎他。他常听说大名鼎鼎的约翰·伦道夫，因此尽心尽力地款待他。

paragraphs.en: A fine supper was prepared, and the innkeeper himself waited upon his guest. John Randolph ate in silence. The innkeeper spoke of the weather, of the roads, of the crops, of politics. But his surly guest said scarcely a word.
paragraphs.zh: 一顿丰盛的晚餐准备好了，客栈老板亲自伺候客人。约翰·伦道夫一言不发地吃着。老板聊天气、聊道路、聊庄稼、聊政治，可这位阴沉的客人几乎一句话也不说。

paragraphs.en: In the morning a good breakfast was served, and then Mr. Randolph made ready to start on his journey. He called for his bill and paid it. His horse was led to the door, and a servant helped him to mount it.
paragraphs.zh: 早晨，一顿丰盛的早餐端了上来，随后伦道夫先生准备上路。他叫来账单，付了钱。马被牵到门口，一个仆人扶他上马。

paragraphs.en: As he was starting away, the friendly innkeeper said, "Which way will you travel, Mr. Randolph?"
paragraphs.zh: 他正要出发时，友善的客栈老板问：“伦道夫先生，您要走哪条路？”

paragraphs.en: Mr. Randolph looked at him in no gentle way, and answered, "Sir!"
paragraphs.zh: 伦道夫先生毫不客气地看了他一眼，答道：“先生！”

paragraphs.en: "I only asked which way you intend to travel," said the man.
paragraphs.zh: “我只是问您打算走哪条路。”那人说。

paragraphs.en: "Oh! I have I paid you my bill?"
"Then, I intend to travel the way I wish to go—do you understand?"
paragraphs.zh: “那么，我打算走我想走的路——你明白吗？”

paragraphs.en: He turned his horse and rode away. He had not gone farther than to the end of the innkeeper's field, when to his surprise he found that the road forked. He did not know whether he should take the right-hand fork or the left-hand.
paragraphs.zh: 他调转马头，骑走了。还没走出客栈老板的田地，他就惊讶地发现路分成了两条岔路。他不知道该走右边那条还是左边那条。

paragraphs.en: He paused for a while. There was no signboard to help him. He looked back and saw the innkeeper still standing by the door. He called to him:"My friend, which of these roads shall I travel to go to Lynchburg?"
paragraphs.zh: 他停了一会儿。没有路标可以帮他。他回头一看，客栈老板还站在门口。他喊道：“朋友，去林奇堡该走哪条路？”

paragraphs.en: "Mr. Randolph," answered the innkeeper, "you have paid your bill and don't owe me a cent. Travel the way you wish to go. Good-by!"
paragraphs.zh: “伦道夫先生，”客栈老板回答，“您付了账，一分钱也不欠我。您想走哪条路就走哪条路吧。再见！”

paragraphs.en: As bad luck would have it, Mr. Randolph took the wrong road. He went far out of his way and lost much time, all on account of his surliness.
paragraphs.zh: 也真是倒霉，伦道夫先生走错了路。他绕了很远，浪费了许多时间，全怪他自己脾气太坏。
